reason: The problem is real and verified verbatim, but the proposed fix is wrong in three of its four strings, so this is a correct problem with a wrong fix. What checks out: lately.html:662-664 and 688-689 carry exactly the quoted strings; "we" occurs exactly once in the whole file (line 688, the ghost heading) — a word-boundary grep for we, our and us returns that one hit; the caption is genuinely the lowercase back half of a sentence split across t-head and t-small; and the ghost (a sibling of .limits, no reference to any tile) never names which refusal it draws. The register charge is not taste: the audience is defined as "the 80% not in", the repo contract makes no-jargon a first-contact gate with an automated language check, and the paid-for defect library already carries "The studio's private vocabulary in the accessibility tree — raised three separate times in one engagement; internal names are not product names" (lessons.md:306). "Has no callers yet" is a code term for a function with no call sites. Nothing here restates a gate assertion: interaction-check.mjs:390-407 asserts tile count, ghost column count, ghost height and heading rank — structure only, never copy. Severity is correctly classed defect, not overstated. Two things are wrong on the seat's side. First, the Element says "in every state", but movementThree() is called in four of seven states (full, partial, quiet, first-run) and is absent from empty, loading and error (lately.html:743-805). Second and decisive, the fix: (a) "This is the chart that will appear here" converts a refusal into an unconditional delivery promise for a writer that plan.html:304-305 says sits behind SIGNAL_ANALYTICS_SNAPSHOTS_ENABLED, default off, and has never run — the protected object is "the trend the product cannot produce is drawn as the chart it would be", conditional, and plan.html:551-553 calls refusing it "the honesty proof for everything else on the page". Promising it is a worse fault than the jargon it replaces. (b) "counted for three weeks running" hardens a vague number into a specific wrong one: plan.html:805 puts the state trend at "roughly thirty days after phase 2", and the three-prior-periods threshold the current copy borrowed belongs to completion_pace_change, a different metric on a sixteen-week clock (plan.html registry:163). (c) "{recordStart}" names a value that does not exist — fixture.js binds readingDate, owner, workspace, slug and openCount and nothing else — and no honest value exists to bind: the reading is 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026, while plan.html says the date recorder shipped 17 Aug, default off, so at this reading dates are not being recorded at all and "Dates have only been recorded since X" would state something false. The existing "switched on in August" carries the same future-dated fault; the fix inherits it instead of catching it. Also "Anything moved before then is not in it" leaves "it" with no antecedent, and "so this cannot count them" keeps the same unnamed "this" the seat objects to in tile three.
sharpenedFix: Keep the seat's tile one nearly as written; replace the other three. Tile one: "Nothing was written down about how much was open in earlier weeks, so there is nothing yet to compare this against." Tile two, which must not name a start date the fixture cannot supply and must not claim recording has begun: "When a date gets moved, nothing keeps a record of it yet. Once something does, only moves from that day on will be in it — anything moved before is gone for good." Tile three: "Notes doesn't keep a list of which decisions are still open, so nothing here can count them. That would be a change in Notes." Ghost heading, conditional, no promise and no first person: "This is the chart that would go here." Ghost caption as one whole sentence in one type role, with the plan's real threshold rather than an invented one: "Once open work starts being counted each week, it fills in after about a month." Attribute the ghost by putting tile one's title on the ghost card as a label — reuse the existing "Not yet" label role with the text "Open work over time" rather than adding a second t-head, so heading rank is untouched. Two things to do at the same time or the rewrite cements a gap: LIMITS is a flat constant and movementThree() takes no arguments, so the partial state does not vary tile two even though plan.html:693 requires the date-movement refusal to change its sentence to name the real cause when Timeline did not answer — take a { partial } argument while the strings are being rewritten. And whatever replaces "in August", make it consistent with the 16 July 2026 reading date or the surface states a recorder that switches on in its own future.
breaks: Copy length changes .limit card heights in a three-across row — re-measure ragged or unequal tile heights and clipping at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440, since tile two gets longer. Collapsing the ghost caption to one sentence removes the t-small dim line beneath t-head; if the caption changes type role, audit.mjs must be re-run for the type ramp, leading and WCAG AA contrast of the new role against the ghost card's composited backdrop. Adding a label to .ghost adds a node inside the card: interaction-check.mjs:405-407 asserts ghostColumns >= 8 and ghostHeight > 80, and at 390px the extra line can push the plot under the 80px floor — re-run the behaviour gate at every width, not just 1440. The same check asserts limits.heading === m1Heading for rank parity, so the ghost label must not be a second t-sect or t-head. Re-shoot all ten frames afterwards; movement three renders in full, partial, quiet and first-run, so four of the seven state shots change, and frames.json is regenerated from them. No palette, weight or family is touched, so the colour and type locks are unaffected.
